title: Reproduce with the two real accounts involved, not root
explanation: As `batchjob`, create a file in `/srv/shared/dropbox`; then, as the unrelated `otherjob` account, try to remove it. It succeeds -- an ordinary, unprivileged account can delete a file it doesn't own in this directory, which is exactly the reported symptom (handoff files vanishing before they're picked up). Testing as root here would be meaningless, since root can always unlink anything regardless of what's misconfigured.

title: Check what the directory's mode actually permits
explanation: `ls -ld /srv/shared/dropbox` shows `drwxrwxrwx root root` -- mode `0777`. World-writable is necessary here, since every job account needs to be able to drop files in -- but by itself it says nothing about who can *remove* a file someone else created. Write permission on a directory covers both creating and deleting entries in it, with no distinction by file ownership.

title: Recognize the missing piece: the sticky bit
explanation: This is the identical problem `/tmp` solves system-wide -- `ls -ld /tmp` shows a trailing `t` instead of the usual `x`. With the sticky bit set on a directory, the kernel restricts removal/rename of a file to: the file's owner, the directory's owner, or root -- regardless of how permissive the directory's own write bits are for everyone else. Without it, `0777` is write-open to deletion by anyone, not just creation.

title: Apply it
explanation: `sudo chmod +t /srv/shared/dropbox` sets the bit. `ls -ld` should now show `drwxrwxrwt` -- the trailing `t` replacing the `x` in the "other" execute position.

title: Verify with the same two real accounts
explanation: As `batchjob`, create a new file; as `otherjob`, attempt to `rm` it. It should now fail with `Operation not permitted`, whereas the identical attempt in step 1 silently succeeded. Confirming with the actual unprivileged accounts matters -- root bypasses the sticky bit exactly as it bypasses everything else, so a root-based check would never have shown the fix taking effect.
